dedupe_keys.name: predicting hurricane induced building damage using multimodal data insights from the steer dataset

description: Predicting Hurricane-Induced Building Damage Using Multimodal Data: Insights from the StEER Dataset is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Danrong Zhang, Georgia Institute of Technology (gatech.edu). This dataset provides a valuable resource for research on hurricane-induced building damage prediction by offering pre-hurricane imagery for buildings impacted by Hurricanes Harvey, Florence, Michael, Sally, and Laura, as documented in the NSF-funded StEER dataset. Coverage: Texas, North Carolina, U.S. Gulf coast, Louisiana, Florida. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Hurricane-induced building damage prediction,  pre-hurricane building images, machine learning, multimodal learning. Published 2025-01-24. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
